title: [Feature][v0.32.0] Add FP8 LI cache support for CANN KeyPool
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backports #18447 to `releases/v0.32.0rc`: adds FP8 LI pooled-key caches with FP32 per-pool scales for GLM-5.3-Flash CANN KeyPool on Ascend 950. BF16 remains the default.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Enables `attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`; SFA precision remains independently configurable. FP8 LI does not support KV offloading.

### How was this patch tested?

147 focused CPU cases passed with CANN/NPU calls mocked, covering hardware capability checks, BF16 bypass, empty/padded queries and scale/padded-stride kernel arguments. UTs were extended in `test_glm5next_kpool_model_backend.py` and `test_cann_keypool_adapters.py`.

The existing FP8 implementation is unchanged by the UT update. The separate A5 regression run is reported below.

**A5 operator regression (2026-11-01):** [singlecard-ops-a5 run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41269132959/job/124739022759) tested head `1b799808133c8e7d9befd0dcf75a71ae22696c50` with vLLM `v0.32.0` on Ascend 950DT using the main CI image: **CANN 9.2.1 / Triton-Ascend 3.2.2 / torch-npu 2.10.0.post4**. All **16** cases in `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_glm5next_cann_keypool.py` passed (**8 FP8 + 8 BF16, 0 skipped**), covering values/scales (including zero vectors), invalid slots, shared/padded pages, tail guards, speculative writes and eager/graph replay.

This run does **not** validate the release-required **Triton-Ascend 3.6.0.post2 / torch-npu 2.10.0.post7** dependencies; no matching-dependency rerun was performed. Although GitHub reports job success, the raw log records a SparseFlashMLA metadata test failure and lacks the final pytest group summary, so only the observed 16-case result is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage.
- [x] Error / failure path coverage.
- [x] Meaningful tests for hardware capability checks, cache layout and BF16 compatibility.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
